page: Amazon Web Services c9g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture, it features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 64 KB L1D cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a 48 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with the Geekbench single-core score of 2385.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 36.44 GB/sec placing in the top tier. Passmark memory score of 3604.52 also ranks in the top tier, reflecting efficient memory subsystem performance. Multi-core and multi-threaded operations, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance at 16026.86 and software compilation with Clang at 21523.0, fall within the average range. Tradeoffs are visible in cryptography and prompt processing for larger models; the Passmark CPU encryption test at 2388.61 and prompt processing for a medium 7B LLM model at 22.52 tokens/sec perform in the lower tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c9g.2xlarge offers a high-density ARM64 compute profile with dedicated cores, avoiding the overhead of hyperthreading. This makes it highly suitable for compute-bound workloads that benefit from strong single-thread execution and high memory performance, such as text processing, web serving, and lightweight LLM text generation. It is also well-suited for general-purpose application hosting, software compilation, and database operations that do not require local NVMe storage.
